html:
The 1971 JVP insurrection was an armed rising in April 1971 by the Janatha Vimukthi Peramuna (JVP, People's Liberation Front), a Marxist party of young, mostly rural Sinhalese, against Sirimavo Bandaranaike's government.

Many rebels were jobless school leavers. On 5 April they attacked police stations across the island and held parts of the south and centre for some weeks. The government, with arms from India, Britain, the Soviet Union and others, crushed them. Thousands died, many killed after capture.

The JVP rose again from 1987 to 1989, during the civil war, and was put down even more brutally. It later turned to elections. In 2024 its leader Anura Kumara Dissanayake won the presidency, after the crisis of 2022.
sum: The 1971 JVP insurrection was an armed rising in April 1971 by the Janatha Vimukthi Peramuna (JVP, People's Liberation Front), a Marxist party of young, mostly rural Sinhalese, against Sirimavo Bandaranaike's government.
